# Source classification: TASVEG {#sec-source}

In this workflow, the source classification is **TASVEG**, the comprehensive digital vegetation map and classification system for Tasmania, including sub-Antarctic Macquarie Island [@TASVEG_3; @TASVEG_5].

The TASVEG dataset combines both ecological descriptions and spatial polygon geometries. For cross-referencing purposes, we distinguish between **mapping units** (polygons coded by `VEGCODE` on the map) and **vegetation communities** (the ecological entities defined in the classification).

The majority of TASVEG mapping units represent distinct ecological vegetation communities—spanning coastal heathlands, wet and dry eucalypt forests, temperate rainforests, moorlands, wetlands, and alpine communities. The companion *Technical Manual* [@KitchenerHarris_2013] provides structured, literature-referenced ecological descriptions for each of the **159 mapping units** defined in TASVEG, covering floristics, structure, environmental drivers, and disturbance regimes.

::: {.callout-note}
## 159 lookup codes vs. 156 mapped statewide polygon units
The TASVEG 5.0 Fire Attributes DBF lookup table (`TASVEG_5_0_Fire_Attributes_LUT.dbf`) and Technical Manual list **159 unique `VEGCODE` entries**. Three of those codes (`FPL`, `HUE`, and `SLW`) do not occur as polygons in the statewide shapefile (`TASVEG_5_0.shp`), which contains **156 unique mapped `VEGCODE` units** (153 eligible vegetation communities plus 3 non-eligible natural mapping units; see @sec-alignment and @sec-lookup).
:::

## Components of TASVEG used in this workflow

TASVEG provides several distinct resources that enter at different stages of the computational pipeline:

- **Technical Manual** (*From Forest to Fjaeldmark*; @KitchenerHarris_2013): supplies the diagnostic ecological descriptions used to assess conceptual alignment (@sec-alignment) and served as the primary ecological reference for all five expert interpreters during Rounds 1 and 2.
- **TASVEG 5.0 statewide spatial release** from <https://www.theLIST.tas.gov.au> ©State of Tasmania [@TASVEG_5]:
  - **Fire attributes lookup table (`.dbf`)**: used in @sec-lookup to construct the authoritative source `lookup_tbl` without needing to load the full polygon geometries first.
  - **Statewide vector spatial data (`.shp` and MapInfo formats)**: used in @sec-areas and @sec-maps (and in the separate output-generation scripts in @sec-outputs) to compute polygon areas and generate GeoPackage and GeoTIFF outputs.
  - **Official metadata (`.pdf`)**: documents attribute definitions, coordinate reference system (`GDA94 / MGA zone 55`, `EPSG:28355`), and release notes.

## Data download and attribution

TASVEG 5.0 data is supplied under the Creative Commons Attribution 3.0 Australia ([CC BY 3.0 AU](http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/au/)) licence.

The Department of Natural Resources and Environment Tasmania requests attribution in the following form:

> “TASVEG 5.0 from www.theLIST.tas.gov.au ©State of Tasmania”

Because the statewide shapefile archive is large and redistributed directly by theLIST Open Data, `gisdata/` is excluded from Git version control. The standalone script below (`scripts/TASVEG-data-download.R`) checks for the local `gisdata/` directory, downloads `LIST_TASVEG_50_STATEWIDE.zip` via `wget`, and extracts the shapefile and DBF lookup tables into `gisdata/LIST_TASVEG_50_STATEWIDE/`. Expand the code block to inspect it (not executed during book rendering):

```{r}
#| filename: "scripts/TASVEG-data-download.R"
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Script to download TASVEG 5.0 data"
#| file: ../../scripts/TASVEG-data-download.R
```

Execution time and R session benchmarking details for this download script are recorded in @sec-reproducibility.
